newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: DMGB NZ sees fiscal contraction in 1999/2000.
newsitem.headline: DMGB NZ sees fiscal contraction in 1999/2000.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMGB) said on Thursday that with no further tax cuts and modest spending increases planned for 1999/2000, the government's fiscal stance would become contractionary in that year.
DMGB, in releasing its "Fiscal Indicator" said the term fiscal expansion was a misnomer for the planned NZ$5.0 billion in extra spending.
The indicator suggested that, taking the next three years together, the fiscal stance would remain broadly unchanged.
"That suggests that the term 'fiscal expansion' is a misnomer for the planned NZ$5.0 billion package of extra government expenditures," DMGB's New Zealand Chief economist Ulf Schoefisch said.
"Rather than leading to an expansion in the size of the government's role in the economy, the extra expenditure will prevent a renewed fiscal contraction that would have otherwise occurred," he said.
He said the DMGB Fiscal indicator showed the significant fiscal expansion in 1996/7 which was primarily driven by the government's tax reduction and social policy programme.

"The extra expenditure initiatives planned for 1997/8 imply a broadly unchanged fiscal stance, followed by a renewed expansion in 1998/99 on the back of the second round of personal income tax cuts," he said.
"With no further tax reductions and relatively modest expenditure increases planned for 1999/2000, the fiscal stance will become contractionary again in that year," Schoefisch said.

DMGB forecast the change in fiscal stance, as a percentage of nominal GDP, would rise by 2.4 percent in the year to June 1997, 0.12 percent in 1997/8, 1.15 percent in 1998/9 and contract by 0.93 percent in 1999/90.
